plan.planning_summary: Refining route_02 to fix compilation failure caused by material identifier truncation ('si' instead of 'sio2'). This iteration repairs the material registry compatibility while preserving the dual-cavity Fabry-Perot scientific hypothesis. Three routes are proposed: (1) corrected dual-cavity with proper IR dielectric materials Ge/ZnS, (2) single-cavity baseline for comparison, and (3) expanded three-cavity design for improved band shaping. All routes widen thickness initialization bounds by ±25%, disable strict optical-margin pruning during candidate generation, and request 50-sample diagnostic batches to identify which physical constraints reject candidates.

routes.title: Corrected Dual-Cavity Fabry-Perot Filter with Ge/ZnS Material Pair
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A two-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter using Germanium (high-index) and Zinc Sulfide (low-index) dielectric materials on CaF2 substrate can achieve high transmittance in both CO (4.55-4.75 μm) and CO2 (4.15-4.35 μm) bands while blocking 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm, with total layer count ≤24.
routes.design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot filter with alternating quarter-wave Bragg reflectors separated by spacer cavities tuned to dual passband centers. Computational optimization adjusts layer thicknesses from quarter-wave initialization to achieve square passband profile with strong out-of-band blocking.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | Bragg reflector (6 layers Ge/ZnS) | Cavity spacer 1 (ZnS) | Bragg reflector (4 layers Ge/ZnS) | Cavity spacer 2 (ZnS) | Bragg reflector (6 layers Ge/ZnS) | Air, total 19 finite layers
soft_objectives: maximize average transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize average transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize average transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize average transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: conventional IR dielectric materials Ge and ZnS are depositable by thermal evaporation or sputtering
total film thickness should remain under 10 μm for stress management
theory_basis: Fabry-Perot interference condition: maximum transmittance when (φ1 + φ2 - 2δ)/2 = kπ
Quarter-wave stack reflectivity increases with layer pair count
Multi-cavity coupling shapes passband from triangular to square profile
expected_advantages: Ge/ZnS pair has high index contrast (~4.0 vs ~2.2 in mid-IR) enabling fewer layers for required blocking
Dielectric-only design avoids metal absorption losses (15-30% reduction in transmittance)
19 layers leaves margin under 24-layer constraint for optimization flexibility
known_risks: Ge has absorption edge near 1.8 μm but should be transparent in 3.5-5.2 μm range - must verify dispersion model
Stress mismatch between Ge and ZnS may cause film cracking if total thickness exceeds practical limits
Fabrication tolerance sensitivity increases with layer count and index contrast
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 19-layer dual-cavity Fabry-Perot infrared bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate. Layer stack: CaF2 | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | ZnS (cavity 1) | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | ZnS (cavity 2) | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Air. Use Germanium and Zinc Sulfide as dielectric materials with proper material registry identifiers. Initialize all layer thicknesses at quarter-wave optical thickness centered at 4.45 μm, then apply ±25% uniform bounds expansion for optimization search. Generate 50 candidate samples with disabled strict optical-margin pruning during candidate generation. Log which physical constraint filters reject candidates. Optimize for high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm bands, low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm bands. Normal incidence, air ambient. Report thicknesses_nm, best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, and run_status. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Repair compilation failure from route_02: material identifier 'si' was truncated incorrectly, should use proper registry names for Ge and ZnS. Widen thickness initialization bounds by ±25%, disable strict optical-margin pruning, generate 50-sample diagnostic batch to identify constraint rejection causes.

routes.title: Single-Cavity Fabry-Perot Baseline for Dual-Band Comparison
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A single-cavity Fabry-Perot filter with 13 layers can achieve acceptable dual-band transmittance but with lower out-of-band blocking than dual-cavity design, providing a baseline to quantify the benefit of added cavity complexity.
routes.design_principle: Single-cavity Fabry-Perot with symmetric Bragg reflectors on both sides of one spacer cavity. Simpler topology reduces optimization complexity and fabrication sensitivity but may not achieve square passband profile.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | Bragg reflector (6 layers Ge/ZnS) | Cavity spacer (ZnS) | Bragg reflector (6 layers Ge/ZnS) | Air, total 13 finite layers
soft_objectives: maximize average transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize average transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize average transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize average transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: Ge and ZnS are conventional IR dielectrics
lower total thickness reduces stress concerns
theory_basis: Single-cavity Fabry-Perot produces triangular passband profile
Bragg reflector pair count determines out-of-band blocking strength
Cavity thickness determines passband center wavelength
expected_advantages: Fewer layers reduces fabrication complexity and tolerance sensitivity
Lower total thickness improves mechanical stability
Provides baseline to quantify dual-cavity benefit
known_risks: Single cavity may not achieve sufficiently square passband for dual-band application
Out-of-band blocking may be weaker than dual-cavity design
May not meet both CO and CO2 band requirements simultaneously

routes.title: Three-Cavity Fabry-Perot for Enhanced Passband Shaping
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A three-cavity Fabry-Perot filter with 23 layers can achieve superior passband flatness and out-of-band blocking compared to dual-cavity design, at the cost of increased fabrication sensitivity and total thickness.
routes.design_principle: Three-cavity Fabry-Perot with coupled resonators produces flatter passband top and steeper band edges. Uses remaining layer budget (23 of 24 max) to maximize blocking performance.
routes.proposed_topology: CaF2 substrate | Bragg reflector (5 layers) | Cavity 1 | Bragg reflector (4 layers) | Cavity 2 | Bragg reflector (4 layers) | Cavity 3 | Bragg reflector (5 layers) | Air, total 23 finite layers
soft_objectives: maximize average transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
maximize average transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
minimize average transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
minimize average transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: 23 layers near 24-layer maximum - minimal margin for adjustment
Ge and ZnS are conventional IR dielectrics
total thickness may approach 10 μm limit - monitor stress
theory_basis: Multi-cavity coupling produces square passband profile with flat top
Additional cavities increase out-of-band blocking without adding reflector layers
Evidence shows 24-layer 4-cavity filter achieved ~100% transmittance with 339 nm FWHM
expected_advantages: Flatter passband top improves transmission uniformity across both target bands
Steeper band edges improve separation between passbands and stopbands
Maximum layer utilization for best possible blocking performance
known_risks: 23 layers near manufacturing limit - minimal tolerance for thickness errors
Higher fabrication sensitivity may cause measured performance to deviate from design
Total thickness may exceed practical stress limits for CaF2 substrate

research_influence: Evidence from CorpusId:237542117 confirms Ge/ZnS material pair is appropriate for mid-IR 3-5 μm filters with high index contrast and low absorption - this directly informs material selection in all three routes
Evidence from CorpusId:139773493 and CorpusId:237542117 supports multi-cavity Fabry-Perot design for square passband profile - this justifies the dual and triple cavity topologies
Evidence from CorpusId:237542117 shows 24-layer 4-cavity filter achieved ~100% transmittance - this validates using up to 23 layers in route_02_refine_03
Prior iteration failure (material identifier truncation) directly motivated the explicit material registry name requirement in all execution requests
unresolved_decisions: Whether Ge absorption in 3.5-5.2 μm range is truly negligible - requires verification from material dispersion model in solver
Optimal cavity count (1 vs 2 vs 3) for this specific dual-band requirement - will be determined by comparing best_target_score across the three routes
Whether 24-layer maximum is a hard fabrication limit or can be relaxed if three-cavity design shows clear benefit
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
